Current efforts have explored the balance between G proteins and β-arrestin; however, other transducers like GPCR kinases (GRKs) remain understudied. GRK2 is essential for β<sub>2</sub> adrenergic receptor (β<sub>2</sub>AR)-mediated glucose uptake, but β<sub>2</sub>AR agonists are considered poor clinical candidates for glycemic management due to G<sub>s</sub>/cyclic AMP (cAMP)-induced cardiac side effects and β-arrestin-dependent desensitization. Using ligand-based virtual screening and chemical evolution, we developed pathway-selective agonists of β<sub>2</sub>AR that prefer GRK coupling. These compounds perform well in preclinical models of hyperglycemia and obesity and demonstrate a lower potential for cardiac and muscular side effects compared with standard β<sub>2</sub>-receptor agonists and incretin mimetics, respectively. Furthermore, the lead candidate showed favorable pharmacokinetics and was well tolerated in a placebo-controlled clinical trial. GRK-biased β<sub>2</sub>AR partial agonists are thus promising oral alternatives to injectable incretin mimetics used in the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity.</AbstractText><CopyrightInformation>Copyright © 2025 The Author(s). which commits nurses to making informed and reasoned clinical decisions. The nursing gaze comprises four structuring elements: the severity of the illness, the assessment of functional difficulties, the patient&amp;#8217;s experience of the illness, and how the person copes with it. It is developed through a process of clinical reasoning, in which the knowledge mobilized gives meaning to the collected data and informs the formulation of clinical judgments. Based on these clinical judgments, nursing knowledge is used to select relevant interventions and expected outcomes for each individual. To define and explain the nursing gaze and its place in nursing practice, this article aims to develop the concept of the nursing gaze based on Tanner&amp;#8217;s model of clinical judgment, combined with nursing theories, and its associated evaluation grid.</AbstractText></Abstract><AuthorList CompleteYN="Y"><Author ValidYN="Y"><LastName>Garry-Bruneau</LastName><ForeName>Mathilde</ForeName><Initials>M</Initials></Author><Author ValidYN="Y"><LastName>Dallaire</LastName><ForeName>Clémence</ForeName><Initials>C</Initials></Author></AuthorList><Language>fre</Language><PublicationTypeList><PublicationType UI="D004740">English Abstract</PublicationType><PublicationType UI="D016428">Journal Article</PublicationType></PublicationTypeList><VernacularTitle>Le regard infirmier au cœur du jugement clinique : une proposition pour situer la pratique infirmière.</VernacularTitle></Article><MedlineJournalInfo><Country>France</Country><MedlineTA>Rech Soins Infirm</MedlineTA><NlmUniqueID>9715370</NlmUniqueID><ISSNLinking>0297-2964</ISSNLinking></MedlineJournalInfo><CitationSubset>IM</CitationSubset><MeshHeadingList><MeshHeading><DescriptorName UI="D006801" MajorTopicYN="N">Humans</DescriptorName></MeshHeading><MeshHeading><DescriptorName UI="D007600" MajorTopicYN="Y">Judgment</DescriptorName></MeshHeading><MeshHeading><DescriptorName UI="D000086723" MajorTopicYN="Y">Clinical Reasoning</DescriptorName></MeshHeading><MeshHeading><DescriptorName UI="D009742" MajorTopicYN="N">Nursing Theory</DescriptorName></MeshHeading></MeshHeadingList><OtherAbstract Type="Publisher" Language="fre"><AbstractText>Cet article d&amp;#233;veloppe le concept du &amp;#171;&amp;#160;regard infirmier&amp;#160;&amp;#187; qui engage les infirmi&amp;#232;res &amp;#224; prendre des d&amp;#233;cisions cliniques de fa&amp;#231;on &amp;#233;clair&amp;#233;e et argument&amp;#233;e. ValidYN="Y">10.1182/blood.2024026040</ELocationID><Abstract><AbstractText>Differentiation arrest and dependence on oxidative metabolism are features shared among genetically diverse acute myeloid leukemias (AMLs). A phenotypic CRISPR-CRISPR-associated protein 9 screen in AML identified dependence on phosphoseryl-transfer RNA kinase (PSTK), an atypical kinase required for the biosynthesis of all selenoproteins. In vivo, PSTK inhibition (PSTKi) impaired AML cell growth and leukemic stem cell self-renewal. Notably, timed pharmacologic PSTKi effectively targeted chemotherapy-resistant AML in murine and patient-derived xenograft models, showing selectivity for malignant cells over normal hematopoietic cells. Mechanistically, PSTKi-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) triggering mitochondrial DNA release into the cytosol and activated cyclic GMP-AMP Synthase-Stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING). This activation, in turn, disrupted iron metabolism, augmenting ROS generation, and amplifying ferroptosis. Together, these findings reveal a self-reinforcing PSTK-cGAS-STING-ROS loop, culminating in an oxidative crisis and ferroptotic cell death of leukemic stem cells. These data highlight the potential for augmenting standard cancer chemotherapies using timed metabolic intervention to eliminate chemotherapy-persisting cells and thereby impede disease relapse.</AbstractText><CopyrightInformation>© 2025 American Society of Hematology. In Madagascar, despite a context marked by deep regional disparities, this approach remains insufficiently documented. This study seeks to assess the impact of territorial health policies on maternal and child health indicators at the national level.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="METHODS" NlmCategory="METHODS">The study is based on secondary analysis of data from the 2021 Demographic and Health Survey. The indicators analyzed cover nutrition, morbidity, reproductive and maternal health, examined at the regional level among children under five years of age and women aged 15 to 49. Chi-square tests-standard or Monte Carlo (10,000 simulations)-with Bonferroni correction, were used to assess regional heterogeneity at a 5% significance level.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="RESULTS" NlmCategory="RESULTS">Regional disparities were statistically significant for most indicators (p&amp;lt;0.001). Stunting reached 51.9% [47.3-56.5] in Vakinankaratra compared to 21.7% [15.3-28.1] in Diana. Vaccination coverage ranged from 81.9% [73.1-90.7] in Itasy to 24.9% [17.6-32.2] in Sava. Institutional deliveries ranged from 68.8% [65.9-71.7] in Analamanga to 14.9% [10.12-19.5] in Ihorombe. Adolescent fertility reached 50.4% [44.5-56.3] in Sofia versus 17.5% [14.5-20.5] in Analamanga.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="DISCUSSION" NlmCategory="CONCLUSIONS">Health decentralization in Madagascar has struggled to reduce regional inequalities, highlighting a persistent gap between national policies and local realities. Indicators reveal significant disparities in nutrition, access to healthcare, contraception, and maternal health. The decentralized territorial communities, often deprived of resources and real autonomy, remain dependent on the central government. The lack of effective territorialization limits the adaptation of policies to local needs. A structural reform is needed, based on the genuine transfer of responsibilities, the strengthening of local capacities, and the co-construction of actions with communities.</AbstractText></Abstract><AuthorList CompleteYN="Y"><Author ValidYN="Y"><LastName>Bemanana</LastName><ForeName>Hery Health</DescriptorName></MeshHeading></MeshHeadingList><OtherAbstract Type="Publisher" Language="fre"><AbstractText Label="INTRODUCTION" NlmCategory="BACKGROUND">La territorialisation des services de santé vise à adapter les politiques sanitaires aux spécificités locales, dans une optique de réduction des inégalités. À Madagascar, malgré un contexte marqué par de profondes disparités régionales, cette approche reste insuffisamment documentée. La présente étude se propose d’évaluer l'impact des politiques de territorialisation sur les indicateurs de santé maternelle et infantile à l’échelle nationale. Méthodes : L’étude repose sur une analyse secondaire des données de l’Enquête Démographique et de Santé 2021. Les indicateurs couvrent la nutrition, la morbidité, la santé reproductive et maternelle, analysés régionalement chez les enfants de moins de cinq ans et les femmes de 15 à 49 ans. Des tests du Chi-deux, classiques ou de Monte Carlo (10 000 simulations), avec correction de Bonferroni, ont mesuré l’hétérogénéité régionale avec un niveau de signification de 5 %. Résultats : Les disparités régionales sont statistiquement significatives pour la majorité des indicateurs (p &lt; 0,001). Le retard de croissance atteint 51,9 % (47,3–56,5) à Vakinankaratra contre 21,7 % (15,3–28,1) à Diana. La couverture vaccinale varie de 81,9 % (73,1–90,7) à Itasy à 24,9 % (17,6–32,2) à Sava. Les accouchements en établissement vont de 68,8 % (65,9–71,7) à Analamanga à 14,9 % (10,3–19,5) à Ihorombe. La fécondité adolescente atteint 50,4 % (44,5–56,3) à Sofia contre 17,5 % (14,5–20,5) à Analamanga.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="DISCUSSION" NlmCategory="CONCLUSIONS">La décentralisation sanitaire à Madagascar peine à réduire les inégalités régionales, révélant un écart persistant entre politiques nationales et réalités locales. Les indicateurs montrent des disparités marquées en matière de nutrition, d’accès aux soins, de contraception et de santé maternelle. Les collectivités territoriales décentralisées (CTD), souvent privées de ressources et d’autonomie réelle, restent dépendantes de l’État central. L’absence de territorialisation effective limite l’adaptation des politiques aux besoins locaux. Une réforme structurelle est nécessaire, fondée sur le transfert réel de compétences, le renforcement des capacités locales et la co-construction des actions avec les communautés.</AbstractText></OtherAbstract><KeywordList Owner="NOTNLM"><Keyword MajorTopicYN="N">.</Keyword><Keyword MajorTopicYN="N">decentralization</Keyword><Keyword ValidYN="Y">10.1038/s44161-025-00669-3</ELocationID><Abstract><AbstractText>Maturation of human pluripotent stem (hPS) cell-derived cardiomyocytes is critical for their use as a model system. Here we mimic human heart maturation pathways in the setting of hPS cell-derived cardiac organoids (hCOs). Specifically, transient activation of 5' AMP-activated protein kinase and estrogen-related receptor enhanced cardiomyocyte maturation, inducing expression of mature sarcomeric and oxidative phosphorylation proteins, and increasing metabolic capacity. hCOs generated using the directed maturation protocol (DM-hCOs) recapitulate cardiac drug responses and, when derived from calsequestrin 2 (CASQ2) and ryanodine receptor 2 (RYR2) mutant hPS cells exhibit a pro-arrhythmia phenotype. These DM-hCOs also comprise multiple cell types, which we characterize and benchmark to the human heart. Modeling of cardiomyopathy caused by a desmoplakin (DSP) mutation resulted in fibrosis and cardiac dysfunction and led to identifying the bromodomain and extra-terminal inhibitor INCB054329 as a drug mitigating the desmoplakin-related functional defect. These findings establish DM-hCOs as a versatile platform for applications in cardiac biology, disease and drug screening.</AbstractText><CopyrightInformation>© 2025. The Localized Potential Accessibility (LPA) indicator, considered the benchmark indicator for identifying underserved areas, provides an indirect measure of the imbalance between health care supply and demand. The aim of this study is to propose a complementary indicator, based on general practitioners&amp;#8217; acceptance of new patients, in order to better characterize territorial inequalities in access to primary care.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="METHODS" NlmCategory="METHODS">We use original data collected from online medical appointment-booking platforms, covering nearly 12,000 general practitioners and more than two-thirds of the French population. At the municipal level, we compute the Proportion of general practitioners accepting New Patients (PNP), using a methodology comparable to that employed for the LPA.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="RESULTS" NlmCategory="RESULTS">Territorial disparities appear more pronounced when measured using the PNP than when measured using the LPA. Across the different measures of dispersion considered, territorial heterogeneity is two to three times higher with the PNP. Substantial discrepancies are observed between the two indicators: for 8.61% of municipalities (15.35% of the population), the LPA underestimates difficulties in accessing primary care, whereas for 11.19% of municipalities (22.28% of the population), it overestimates them relative to the PNP.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="CONCLUSION" NlmCategory="CONCLUSIONS">The PNP constitutes a direct and concise indicator of the imbalance between health care supply and demand. Complementary to the LPA, it enables a more refined identification of underserved areas and improves the targeting of public policies aimed at reducing territorial inequalities in access to primary care. These findings support broader collection and systematic use of the PNP as a central criterion for analyzing supply&amp;#8211;demand imbalances and as a tool to guide public policy L&amp;#8217;accessibilit&amp;#233; aux soins primaires constitue un enjeu majeur de sant&amp;#233; publique en France. L&amp;#8217;accessibilit&amp;#233; potentielle localis&amp;#233;e (APL), consid&amp;#233;r&amp;#233;e comme l&amp;#8217;indicateur de r&amp;#233;f&amp;#233;rence pour identifier les territoires en tension, fournit une mesure indirecte du d&amp;#233;s&amp;#233;quilibre entre l&amp;#8217;offre et la demande de soins. L&amp;#8217;objectif de cette &amp;#233;tude est de proposer un indicateur compl&amp;#233;mentaire, fond&amp;#233; sur l&amp;#8217;acceptation de nouveaux patients par les m&amp;#233;decins g&amp;#233;n&amp;#233;ralistes, afin de mieux caract&amp;#233;riser les in&amp;#233;galit&amp;#233;s territoriales d&amp;#8217;acc&amp;#232;s aux soins. M&amp;#233;thodes&amp;#160;: Nous exploitons des donn&amp;#233;es originales issues de plateformes de prise de rendez-vous m&amp;#233;dicaux en ligne, couvrant pr&amp;#232;s de 12&amp;#160;000 m&amp;#233;decins g&amp;#233;n&amp;#233;ralistes et plus des deux tiers de la population fran&amp;#231;aise. Nous d&amp;#233;terminons, &amp;#224; l&amp;#8217;&amp;#233;chelle communale, la proportion de m&amp;#233;decins g&amp;#233;n&amp;#233;ralistes acceptant de nouveaux patients (PNP), en utilisant une m&amp;#233;thodologie comparable &amp;#224; celle de l&amp;#8217;APL. R&amp;#233;sultats&amp;#160;: Les disparit&amp;#233;s territoriales apparaissent plus marqu&amp;#233;es lorsqu&amp;#8217;elles sont mesur&amp;#233;es par la PNP que par l&amp;#8217;APL. Selon les diff&amp;#233;rentes mesures de dispersion retenues, l&amp;#8217;h&amp;#233;t&amp;#233;rog&amp;#233;n&amp;#233;it&amp;#233; territoriale est deux &amp;#224; trois fois plus &amp;#233;lev&amp;#233;e avec la PNP. Des discordances substantielles sont observ&amp;#233;es entre les deux indicateurs&amp;#160;: pour 8,61 % des communes (15,35 % de la population), l&amp;#8217;APL sous-estime les difficult&amp;#233;s d&amp;#8217;acc&amp;#232;s aux soins, tandis que pour 11,19 % des communes (22,28 % de la population), elle les surestime relativement &amp;#224; la PNP. Conclusion&amp;#160;: La PNP constitue un indicateur direct et synth&amp;#233;tique du d&amp;#233;s&amp;#233;quilibre entre l&amp;#8217;offre et la demande de soins. Compl&amp;#233;mentaire &amp;#224; l&amp;#8217;APL, la PNP permet d&amp;#8217;affiner l&amp;#8217;identification des territoires en tension et de mieux cibler les politiques publiques visant &amp;#224; r&amp;#233;duire les in&amp;#233;galit&amp;#233;s territoriales d&amp;#8217;acc&amp;#232;s aux soins. previously developed an approach to calibrate computational tools for clinical variant classification, updating recommendations for the reliable use of variant impact predictors to provide evidence strength up to Strong. A new generation of tools using distinctive approaches has since been released, and these methods must be independently calibrated for clinical application.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="METHODS" NlmCategory="METHODS">Using our local posterior probability-based calibration and our established data set of ClinVar pathogenic and benign variants, we determined the strength of evidence provided by 3 new tools (AlphaMissense, ESM1b, and VARITY) and calibrated scores meeting each evidence strength.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="RESULTS" NlmCategory="RESULTS">All 3 tools reached the Strong level of evidence for variant pathogenicity and Moderate for benignity, although sometimes for few variants. Compared with previously recommended tools, these yielded at best only modest improvements in the trade-offs between evidence strength and false-positive predictions.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="CONCLUSION" NlmCategory="CONCLUSIONS">At calibrated thresholds, 3 new computational predictors provided evidence for variant pathogenicity at similar strength to the 4 previously recommended predictors (and comparable with functional assays for some variants). This calibration broadens the scope of computational tools for application in clinical variant classification. Their new approaches offer promise for future advancement of the field.</AbstractText><CopyrightInformation>Copyright © 2025 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Inc. In recent years, deep learning has demonstrated unique advantages in AMP prediction, surpassing traditional machine learning methods and offering new avenues to address the issue of antibiotic resistance. This review introduces the research foundations of deep learning in AMP prediction, covering data set status, processing methods, and representation learning approaches. It particularly focuses on the application of basic models, language models, graph-related models, and other mixed and multimodal models for AMP prediction from the perspective of algorithmic models. Additionally, this review provides a comparative validation using classic deep learning models, offering guidance for subsequent research. ValidYN="Y">10.1016/j.eclinm.2025.103193</ELocationID><Abstract><AbstractText Label="BACKGROUND" NlmCategory="UNASSIGNED">Haematologic malignancies accounted for 6.6% of total cancer cases and 7.2% of total cancer-related deaths worldwide in 2022. We implemented a novel approach to estimate the lifetime risk of developing and dying from various types of haematologic malignancies at the global, regional and country-specific perspectives in 2022.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="METHODS" NlmCategory="UNASSIGNED">We retrieved incidence and mortality rates for Hodgkin lymphoma (HL), Non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL), multiple myeloma (MM) and leukaemia from GLOBOCAN 2022 of 185 countries, along with the national population statistics and all-cause mortality data sourced from the United Nations. For trend analysis, we obtained consecutive cancer registry data spanning from 2003 to 2017 from the Cancer Incidence in Five Continents (CI5) Plus database. After quality control, datasets from 30 countries were included. We used the "adjusted for multiple primaries (AMP)" method to calculate the lifetime risk of incidence (LRI) and mortality (LRM) by cancer type, selected age interval, sex, country and geographic region.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="FINDINGS" NlmCategory="UNASSIGNED">In 2022, the global lifetime risk of incidence (LRI) and mortality (LRM) for all haematologic malignancies was 1.67% and 0.98%, respectively. LRI was highest for NHL, whereas the LRM was highest for leukaemia. On a general level, males exhibited higher LRI and LRM compared to females. Both LRI and LRM increased with higher Human Development Index (HDI) levels. The LRI and LRM for haematologic malignancies were notably high in regions such as Australia/New Zealand, Northen America, as well as Northen, Western and Southern Europe, whereas they were comparatively low in Middle, Western and Eastern Africa. We observed about 5-fold regional disparity in the LRI/LRM ratio for HL, ranging from 1.50 in Middle Africa to 7.67 in Western Europe. Individuals aged 60 and above still faced 71.26% and 78.57% remaining risks for developing and dying from all haematologic malignancies. Among the 185 countries studied, NHL was the haematologic malignancy with the highest LRI in 68.65% of the countries. However, leukaemia had the highest LRM in 58.92% of these countries. MM exhibited the highest LRI and LRM particularly in islands surrounding the Caribbean Sea. Out of 30 countries with eligible consecutive cancer surveillance data, 24 exhibited significant upward trends in LRI of all haematologic malignancies, with AAPCs ranging from 0.5% in USA to 4.3% in Latvia. 25 countries showed significant upward trends in LRM, with AAPCs ranging from 1.0% in USA to 5.5% in Republic of Korea.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="INTERPRETATION" NlmCategory="UNASSIGNED">The global lifetime risks of haematologic malignancies exhibit considerable variations across different world regions, necessitating country-specific and targeted decision-making strategies. In contrast to traditional indicators, the compositive lifetime risks provide intuitive measures with profound public health implications, offering fresh insights into the development of regional disease prevention and control strategies.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="FUNDING" NlmCategory="UNASSIGNED">CAMS Innovation Funds for Medical Sciences (No. 2021-I2M-1-061, No. Factors</DescriptorName></MeshHeading></MeshHeadingList><OtherAbstract Type="Publisher" Language="fre"><AbstractText Label="INTRODUCTION" NlmCategory="BACKGROUND">En France, les individus de 65 ans et plus présentent des taux de vaccination antigrippale (VAG) inférieurs aux objectifs de santé publique. L’explicitation des facteurs structurels de la VAG peut apporter des informations utiles aux campagnes de prévention. Méthode : Cette recherche s’appuie sur des données agrégées au niveau départemental issues de la statistique publique. Les variations des taux de VAG des individus de 65 ans et plus, entre 2016 et 2022, sont estimées par régressions linéaires multiples selon les évolutions de leurs revenus médians, de leur taux de pauvreté, d’indicateurs de santé et d’activité physique, ainsi que de la disponibilité des médecins généralistes sur les territoires. Afin de contrôler l’hétérogénéité interindividuelle, des effets fixes individuels et temporels sont ajoutés. Des écarts-types robustes sont calculés selon la méthode de White. Résultats : Une augmentation d’un point de leur taux de pauvreté est associée à une diminution du taux de VAG des 65 ans et plus de 1,06 % (p &lt; 0,001) ; une augmentation de leur taux de passage aux urgences pour syndrome grippal d’un cas pour 10 000 est associée à une augmentation de leur taux de VAG la saison suivante de 0,004 % (p &lt; 0,001) ; une amélioration de l’accessibilité aux médecins généralistes d’une consultation par personne et par an est associée à une élévation du taux de VAG des 65 ans et plus d’1,56 % (p &lt; 0,01). L’effet de l’accessibilité diminue à mesure que le revenu médian des 65 ans et plus s’élève (p &lt; 0,001) et que leur santé s’améliore (p &lt; 0,01).</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="CONCLUSIONS" NlmCategory="CONCLUSIONS">Une approche socio-territoriale des facteurs de la VAG des individus âgés peut contribuer à la fois au dimensionnement des politiques de santé publique et, de manière plus modeste, à l’explicitation des ressorts de la VAG.</AbstractText></OtherAbstract><KeywordList Owner="NOTNLM"><Keyword MajorTopicYN="N">influenza</Keyword><Keyword MajorTopicYN="N">local potential accessibility</Keyword><Keyword MajorTopicYN="N">poverty rate</Keyword><Keyword MajorTopicYN="N">vaccination</Keyword></KeywordList></MedlineCitation><PubmedData><History><PubMedPubDate PubStatus="medline"><Year>2026</Year><Month>5</Month><Day>22</Day><Hour>0</Hour><Minute>34</Minute></PubMedPubDate><PubMedPubDate PubStatus="pubmed"><Year>2026</Year><Month>5</Month><Day>22</Day><Hour>0</Hour><Minute>33</Minute></PubM
